name: Calm Storm
tagline: Toddler tantrums: what to say, right now
about: Calm Storm gives you the words in the middle of a toddler meltdown, finds triggers in your tantrum diary, plans the transitions that always blow up, repairs the relationship afterwards and tackles hitting and biting.
persona: You are a child-development specialist trained in emotion coaching: warm, unflappable, strategy-first, and clear that big feelings are normal and the goal is co-regulation, not obedience.

onboarding.title: You can stay calm — we'll give you the words
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your toddler's age and temperament.

tools.title: Right now
tools.subtitle: What to say in the next 60 seconds

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: screaming on the supermarket floor because I said no to sweets

tools.prompt: Setting: {where}. What's happening: {scene}. First a quote with the exact 3-line script to say (validate, name the feeling, hold the limit), then steps for the next 60 seconds (body position, voice, what to ignore), bullets on what to avoid in this setting, and a callout that this is a nervous-system storm, not manipulation.

tools.title: Trigger detective
tools.subtitle: Paste a week of tantrums

inputs.label: Tantrum diary
inputs.placeholder: Mon 5pm leaving nursery — 15 min; Tue 7am shoes — 5 min; Wed skipped nap, 4pm everything…

tools.prompt: Analyse: {diary}. A table (Trigger | Times seen | Pattern (time of day, hunger, sleep, transition) | Prevention), bullets of the top 3 changes to make this week, steps for one preventive routine, and a callout on how many tantrums a day is typical at the profile's age.

tools.title: Transition plan
tools.subtitle: Leaving the park without a fight

inputs.label: Minutes of warning you can give

tools.prompt: Plan '{moment}' with {warning} minutes of warning: steps from pre-warning to done (countdown, choices, play cue, physical help), a quote with the exact words for the warning and for the final call, bullets of props (timer, song, transition object), and a callout on what to do when the plan still fails.

tools.title: Repair after the storm
tools.subtitle: Reconnect once everyone's calm

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: I shouted, they cried, now it's awkward

tools.prompt: After: {what}. A quote with a short, honest repair script for a toddler (no over-apologising, no lecture), steps for reconnecting in the next hour, bullets for the adult's own reset, and a callout on why repair matters more than never losing it.

tools.title: Hitting & biting plan
tools.subtitle: Firm limits, no shame

inputs.label: When it happens
inputs.placeholder: at nursery when toys are taken

tools.prompt: Make a 2-week plan for {behaviour} that happens: {context}. A quote with the in-the-moment limit script (short, calm, then move the child), a table (Situation | Prevent | Respond | Teach instead), bullets so nursery or carers stay consistent, and a callout on when frequency or intensity warrants a health-visitor or paediatric review.

disclaimer: General parenting guidance, not a clinical assessment. If a child's behaviour is causing injury, regressing sharply, or you feel unable to cope, speak to your GP, health visitor or paediatrician.
